props.doc:
Claim, lease, execute, report.

The claim is a conditional database update, so a redelivered containment job
finds the row already claimed and acknowledges without acting. That is where
at-least-once delivery becomes effectively-once execution.
props.name: handle_job

props.doc:
Fail steps whose worker stopped heartbeating.

Deliberately fails rather than re-runs. The retry policy on the node decides
whether a new attempt is created, because silently re-running a step that
may have already isolated a host is the wrong default.
props.name: reap_lost_workers

props.code:
import json

return db.execute(
    "UPDATE execution_step SET status = 'failed', finished_at = now(), "
    "error = %s WHERE org_id = %s AND status = 'running' "
    "AND started_at < now() - (%s || ' seconds')::interval",
    [json.dumps({"error_class": "TRANSIENT", "message": "worker lost"}),
     org_id, str(int(lease_seconds))],
    org_id,
)

props.doc: Register and refresh a worker, which is what makes worker health a dashboard tile rather than a guess.
props.name: heartbeat

props.code:
import os
import socket

db.execute(
    "INSERT INTO worker (id, pool, hostname, pid, version, started_at, "
    "last_heartbeat_at, status) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, now(), now(), 'up') "
    "ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_heartbeat_at = now(), status = 'up'",
    [worker_id, pool, socket.gethostname(), os.getpid(), "0.1.0"],
    "",
)
